page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, provisioned with 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. Supported CPU instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512F, AES-NI, BMI2, and FMA. Memory capacity totals 48.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying on remote block storage, and provides a baseline network throughput of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate distinct divergence between single-core efficiency and multi-core throughput. Single-core performance indicators, such as Geekbench (950.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (19.18 GB/sec), register in weak to poor tiers. Conversely, multi-threaded benchmarks perform solidly in the mid-range: multi-core stress-ng reached 8832.77, multi-core Geekbench reached 4757.0, and PassMark CPU registered 10094.6. Memory throughput is robust under caching (493.3 GB/sec small block) and stabilizes at 57.04 GB/sec read and 48.64 GB/sec write for large uncached transfers. The instance manages 8.86 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves moderate LLM inference speeds on lightweight 135M parameter models (653.12 prompt tokens/sec), but slows down significantly when processing 7B parameter models.

Given its hardware allocation, ecs.g5.3xlarge delivers cost-efficient density for horizontal and parallel workloads rather than low-latency single-thread tasks. The lack of built-in local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU acceleration eliminates overheads for workflows that rely exclusively on network-attached storage and standard compute. Suitable production use cases include enterprise web application serving, backend microservices, moderate database instances, Redis caching nodes, and parallel compilation tasks.
